design: AuthenticatedDeletionCheckpointAuthority implements DeletionCheckpointAuthority: the attestation of the deletion authority is verified (exact True) before the closed canonical RecoveryPointCheckpointClaim is parsed; the claim binds the recovery point URN configured by the restore composition to sequence, head and deletion epoch.

DeletionRestoreGate keeps stable DeletionRecoveryError codes raised by the authority (CHECKPOINT_UNAUTHENTICATED, RECOVERY_POINT_MISMATCH, CHECKPOINT_INVALID) instead of relabelling them; other provider exceptions remain DELETION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE.

RestoredMemorySearch is the composed searchMemory entry point of the restored stores: request and binding are forwarded unchanged through DeletionRestoreGate.serve, which rechecks the checkpoint and every participant's inventory before and after materialisation.

Codex's WIP design is unchanged: hash-chained journal snapshot pinned to the authority checkpoint, MemoryDeletionMetadataReplay of original versions/events/audit refs, RestoredMemoryParticipant adapting 0055 participants with tenant/partition/version binding, gate closed until every obligation is purged and inventoried.
No change to approved architecture, contracts, lifecycle FSM or 0055 participants; deletion.py has no backend client and no canonical authority path.

normative_interpretations: ADD v1.3 Part II §§2.10/2.13 and LLD v1.1 §§2.8.6/5.4: a restored backup may hold deleted items; it is honoured by replaying the authoritative tombstones (completed and unfinished) and purging every restored representation before any retrieval is served, not by rewriting the immutable recovery point.

The checkpoint authority must be independent of the restored backup and of the caller: the deletion authority attests its current journal checkpoint for the specific recovery point (OpenBao transit signature in the qualifying cases); a stale journal at the restore site keeps restore closed (CHECKPOINT_MISMATCH) until the current one is delivered.

Caches/replicas/exports: the runtime has no result cache; a restored replica/export is a RestoredDeletionParticipant and, when recorded by the source saga, must be configured or restore stays closed (DELETION_PARTICIPANT_MISSING).
Requirement ids follow the backlog task (BR-003, FR-118); this is component-level evidence of the restore boundary, not G6 requirement verification.

requirement_results.command: Real recovery point on PostgreSQL 16 (one REPEATABLE READ snapshot copy of every table of the source schema) and Qdrant 1.15.1 (snapshot of every native/parallel collection recovered through the snapshot API into a new namespace), restored after a deletion made in the source: the restored stores really hold the deleted item in every retrieval mode and the parallel representation, yet the restore gate and the composed RestoredMemorySearch entry point refuse every request (RESTORE_NOT_RECONCILED) until the attested checkpoint is reconciled; afterwards no mode serves the item, undeleted and shared-content items are served; a restart with fresh adapters starts closed and reconciliation is idempotent (no replacement ledger event)

On the real backends the restored metadata, ledger, native lexical/vector entries, parallel descriptors and private content objects of the deleted item are purged (shared content retained) and the original versions, epochs, events and audit refs are replayed unchanged; an unfinished (DELETION_INCOMPLETE) source saga is replayed as such and its recorded replica participant must be present (DELETION_PARTICIPANT_MISSING otherwise); when the authority completes its saga the new versions are replayed; conflicting, unbound or other-tenant metadata/bindings are refused before any write

The checkpoint authority is AuthenticatedDeletionCheckpointAuthority: the deletion authority's canonical RecoveryPointCheckpointClaim (recovery point URN derived from the backup manifest digest, sequence, head, deletion epoch) is attested with an OpenBao 2.6.2 transit ed25519 key and verified before parsing; a forged payload or malformed signature (CHECKPOINT_UNAUTHENTICATED), a claim for another recovery point (RECOVERY_POINT_MISMATCH), a non-canonical or extended claim (CHECKPOINT_INVALID) and an authority/verifier outage (DELETION_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE) keep restore closed with nothing purged; only an exact True verification authenticates

The restored deletion journal must reproduce exactly the authority checkpoint (sequence, head, deletion epoch): removed suffix, reorder, rehashed replacement, invalid saga history, malformed chain records or entries and a wrong last entry digest are JOURNAL_CORRUPTED or CHECKPOINT_MISMATCH and never open restore; on the real backends a restore site still holding the journal delivered before a later deletion cannot reconcile (CHECKPOINT_MISMATCH) until the current journal is delivered

A deletion attested after reopening closes the gate (CHECKPOINT_MISMATCH, then RESTORE_NOT_RECONCILED) until the new journal is delivered and reconciled; a Qdrant purge or inventory outage during reconciliation keeps restore closed (DELETION_INCOMPLETE / DELETION_INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE) and a retry opens it; residue or a new epoch appearing while a response is materialised discards it; the module has no backend client and no canonical authority path

residual_risks: Freshness of the attestation is the deletion authority's obligation: AttestedJournal attests on every call, but the gate cannot by itself detect an authority that replays an older valid attestation for the same recovery point; no anti-replay nonce or timestamp is part of the claim (open, unassigned).

The window between the final recheck in serve and the return of the response is not atomic with respect to a concurrent authority append (inherited from Codex's WIP limitation); no FGM-17 claim is made.

A failing restored search request (e.g. an authorisation denial) closes the gate and requires a new reconcile (fail-closed semantics of serve inherited from the WIP); availability impact only, not a disclosure.
The backup is a logical PostgreSQL snapshot copy and Qdrant snapshot recovery inside the test harness; pg_dump/pg_restore and off-host backup media are not exercised by this task.
The ledger and representation receipts of the 0052/0053 world fixture are in-process; they are copied with the backup rather than restored from a durable store.
